aggregate_metrics.ADPR_denominator: All dependency_points unless a paper section explicitly reports primary_async_dependency_ids only.
aggregate_metrics.minimum_success_condition_for_task_level: All primary_async_dependency_ids pass in the final integrated workspace.

annotation_notes: The scaffold_to_dispatch dependency is the primary signal because Flask dispatch is highly sensitive to stale route, endpoint, URL map, and callback registry semantics.
The session_json_to_context dependency captures stale assumptions around JSON response shape, tagged session serialization, and cookie lifecycle.
The context_to_template_testing dependency captures stale context-stack assumptions consumed by templating and FlaskClient helpers.
These labels identify public test-observable contracts, not solution code.

dependency_points.contract_summary: Scaffold and sansio App route registration, endpoint naming, URL map, and callback registries must be stable for Flask request dispatch and URL generation.
dependency_points.resolution_criteria: Resolved when route registration, request dispatch, and URL map probes pass together in the integrated workspace.
dependency_points.stale_failure_mode: The dispatch agent may assume stale endpoint naming, URL map, or callback registry semantics from the scaffold layer.

dependency_points.contract_summary: SessionInterface, SecureCookieSession, TaggedJSONSerializer, and JSONProvider response behavior must be stable for request context open/save and response conversion.
dependency_points.resolution_criteria: Resolved when JSON provider, session cookie, and request-context session probes pass after integration.
dependency_points.stale_failure_mode: The dispatch/context agent may save sessions or convert responses against stale JSON serialization or cookie lifecycle assumptions.

dependency_points.contract_summary: Templating and test client helpers must consume current_app/request/session context, JSON dumps, and response/session behavior consistently.
dependency_points.resolution_criteria: Resolved when app/request context probes, templating context probes, and test-client session probes pass after integration.
dependency_points.stale_failure_mode: The templating/testing agent may build clients or render templates against stale context stack and JSON/session assumptions.

evaluation_checkpoint_policy.minimum_policy: Run probe tests after each agent final artifact and after final integration.
evaluation_checkpoint_policy.recommended_policy: Run probe tests after every committed patch, every explicit artifact transfer, and final integration.

ADPR.definition: Fraction of registered dependency_points whose required integrated_probe_tests pass in the final integrated workspace.
ADPR.name: Async Dependency Pass Rate

CAIL.definition: downstream_resolution_step minus upstream_resolution_step when both probe groups have been evaluated.
CAIL.name: Cross-Agent Integration Lag

DRS.definition: First recorded checkpoint at which all required integrated_probe_tests for a dependency point pass.
DRS.name: Dependency Resolution Step

SAD.definition: Interval during which a downstream worker acts on a contract assumption inconsistent with the latest upstream artifact.
SAD.name: Stale Assumption Duration

purpose: Dependency-level labels for measuring whether asynchronous multi-agent coding resolves Flask scaffold/app, request context, JSON/session, templating, and testing-client contracts.
